title: Why 2/3/4/5 falters where 1/2/3/4 succeeds
summary: Discusses the /fit/ plate standards. He argues 1/2/3/4 (1-plate OHP, 2-plate bench, 3-plate squat, 4-plate deadlift) is a sound novice benchmark because lifts scale with muscle recruitment and absolute loads are low, but 2/3/4/5 and 3/4/5/6 break down because lifts progress at very different rates and leverages start to dominate.

claims.claim: 1/2/3/4 means a 1-plate overhead press (135 lbs), 2-plate bench (225), 3-plate squat (315) and 4-plate deadlift (405); hitting it is said to mark graduation from novice status.
The standards are staggered because lifts that involve more muscle mass (deadlift > squat > bench > OHP) let you fire more of the nervous system and be stronger.
For most lifters 1/2/3/4 holds true: when you hit a one-plate OHP you will be around a two-plate bench and three-plate squat, with variation from leverages.
1/2/3/4 works because absolute loads are low and most people don't start from the empty bar, so the margin of error between lifts stays small.
Lifts recruiting more muscle progress faster, so as loads get heavier the gap between lifts widens; 2/3/4/5 allows too large a percentage discrepancy.
Most people can start overhead pressing around 75-80 lbs, so reaching 135 is modest, but going from 135 to 225 is 90 lbs on a lift that is very hard to progress.
A three-plate bench is far easier to hit than a two-plate overhead press; the claim that they correlate is untrue.
When he had a three-plate bench his overhead press was only around 150 lbs.
In four years of commercial gyms he never saw anyone overhead press 225 lbs.
For lower body lifts leverages dominate: long femurs and a longer torso make a 4-plate squat hard while making deadlifts easier; short-limbed lifters struggle to deadlift 5 plates.
1/2/3/4 is a good standard for novices; 2/3/4/5 is not, and 3/4/5/6 makes even less sense.
Almost nobody can strict press three plates; the ones he knows, natural or not, bench at least 500 lbs and most around 550.
He had a 500 lb deadlift while squatting only around 365, so the squat/deadlift standards didn't correlate for him either.
Beyond novice level leverages play too much of a role to set standards based on fixed numbers.
